subject: Week 35: anchor the furniture — pulling to stand changes the risk map
bodyText:
This week
Receptive language is running ahead of production: he likely understands 10-20 simple words, and production typically lags reception by 1-3 months. Cruising along furniture is consolidating for early movers and pulling to stand keeps improving — both are CDC 12-month checkpoints, so later is still normal. The same cognitive upgrade that finds hidden toys now notices exits, which is why separation protest and a sleep wobble often arrive together around 8-9 months.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] More night wakings and bedtime protest without illness — the 8-9-month sleep disruption typically resolves in 2-4 weeks and often overlaps the shift from three naps to two.
- [low concern] Falls and bumps during cruising practice — pad sharp corners and keep practice zones on forgiving surfaces.
- [monitor] No pulling to stand or cruising yet — not a red flag (CDC checkpoint: 12 months), but worth a line in the 9-month visit notes.
- [call within 24h] Sudden persistent sleep refusal arriving with illness signs — fever, ear-pulling, refusing feeds.
- [call now] Head injury followed by persistent vomiting or lethargy; fever ≥102°F (rectal) with lethargy; labored breathing or blue lips — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Anchor everything tall this week — TV, dressers, bookshelves — and hardware-mount a gate at the top of any stairs. Pulling to stand converts furniture from scenery into load-bearing equipment, and tip-overs are a recurring, preventable cause of infant deaths. AAP: Childproofing Your Home: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-home/Pages/Childproofing-Your-Home.aspx
- Hold the bedtime routine absolutely fixed through the regression: same sequence, same brief response at wakings. Consistency is the intervention; novelty resets the clock. AAP: Getting Your Baby to Sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx
- Sing hand-motion songs — Itsy Bitsy Spider, pat-a-cake — imitation, rhythm, and receptive vocabulary in one activity; pat-a-cake itself is a CDC 1-year checklist item some babies show early. CDC 1-year milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
- Ask two-choice questions at the book — where is the dog, here or here. He answers with gaze before he answers with a point, and both count as comprehension data for the ASQ-3. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/

Upcoming
- Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — window opens in nine days; if it is not booked, book it today.
- Day 250-256 (Jan 16-22, 2027): first-step territory opens for early walkers (full range 9-17 months) — clear the cruising runways now.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Pulls to stand at furniture or your legs
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Time to switch to a lower crib mattress setting if not already.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pulls-to-stand/complete

- Babbles with inflection (sounds like speech)
  AAP window: day 240-330
  What to look for: Jargon. Pitch and rhythm of a sentence without recognizable words.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/babbles-with-inflection/complete

- Explores objects by shaking, banging, throwing, dropping
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Systematic property exploration. Repetitive drops are research, not defiance.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/explores-objects-many-ways/complete

- Lets objects go voluntarily (drops on purpose)
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Controlled release — distinct from accidental dropping. Predecessor to throwing.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/lets-objects-go-voluntarily/complete

- Pokes with index finger
  AAP window: day 240-365
  What to look for: Isolated finger use. Predecessor to pointing.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pokes-with-index/complete
